newsitem.title: INDIA: RBI sees record Indian grain production in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: RBI sees record Indian grain production in 1996/97.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said it expected Indian foodgrains production for the year ending on March 31, 1997, to surpass the historic peak of 191.1 million tonnes achieved in 1994/95 (April-March).

"In view of the favourable monsoon, agricultural harvest during 1996/97 is expected to show a sharp rise in foodgrains production, surpassing the earlier peak level of foodgrains production," RBI said in its "Report on Currency and Finance 1995-96" released on Monday.

It said agriculture had suffered a setback in 1995/96, notwithstanding the eight successive favourable monsoon in the country. Foodgrains production fell to 185.0 million tonnes in 1995/96 from the historic peak of 191.1 million tonnes in 1994/95, the RBI said.

It said late arrival of monsoon, floods in the north-western and eastern parts of the country and a decline in the cultivated area under foodgrains, especially wheat and coarse cereals, were the main factors causing a fall in production in 1995/96.
